content.text: I have enough to conclude. No take-or-pay or minimum volume commitment binds our side.

input.quote: From time to time, the Class A Certificateholder may, solely at its option, deposit amounts into the Acquisition Account, as set forth in Section 2.5 of the Trust Agreement.
input.rationale: The agreement contains no minimum purchase commitment, take-or-pay, shortfall penalty or volume restriction on the Issuer or Depositor, so it sits at the preferred position (no minimum commitment; consideration is paid only for property actually transferred). The closest analogues all cut in our favour or are purely optional: (i) transfers of Additional Receivables under Section 2.1(b)-(d) are conditional (Transfer Notice, Credit Enhancement Test, Pool Composition Tests, Depositor certifications) and consideration equals the Additional Receivables Transfer Amount for receivables actually acquired — the Issuer is nowhere obliged to acquire a minimum volume; (ii) funding of the Acquisition Account and the related Negative Carry Account under Section 4.4(d)(i) and 4.4(c)(i) is made by the Class A Certificateholder "solely at its option", and Required Acquisition Deposit Amount / Required Negative Carry Amount are only internal cash-trapping levels with excesses released back to the Certificateholders, not payments we must make to the counterparty; (iii) the Optional Acquisition and Optional Redemption in Article VIII are options, not obligations, and require full payment of the Notes; and (iv) the only "shortfall" mechanic (Section 4.3(h) Credit Payments) is an obligation of the Marketing Agent to fund us. The $425,000 Additional Successor Servicer Fee floor is a servicing-transition fee for a replacement servicer, not a purchase commitment, and it supports our ability to replace Cellco. No redline required.
